summary.headline: Arvind Fashions Q4 FY26 revenue up 14.8% to INR1,365 crore NSV; FY27 guided to mid-double-digit growth and 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion.
summary.overview: Q4 NSV rose 14.8% YoY to INR1,365 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income at INR189 crore (vs INR159 crore) and a 50 bps margin gain. Reported PAT was INR47 crore against a loss of INR93 crore a year earlier; comparable PAT grew 56%. For FY26, revenue grew 14%, EBITDA margin rose 40 bps to 13.4%, comparable PAT grew 62% to INR124 crore, and ROCE crossed 23%. Direct channels reached 56% of sales, and management guided to mid-double-digit growth and 30-40 bps margin expansion in FY27 despite macro and commodity risks.

segments.name: Retail (offline)
segments.commentary: Q4 retail grew 14% with LTL of 7.8%; PVH brands were hit by a transitory GST slab change to 18% for a few weeks, now back to double-digit growth. FY26 added over 1.4 lakh net sq ft; 50 EBOs added in Q4.

segments.name: Online B2C
segments.commentary: Grew over 40% in Q4, raising share to 14% from 11%, as the company shifts away from B2B online. Management expects online B2C to sustain 20%+ growth over the years.

segments.name: Brands
segments.commentary: USPA posted its highest-ever growth in Q4; PVH brands and Flying Machine each grew over 10% (Flying Machine retail LTL in double digits, B2C up 70%). Arrow was subdued due to a one-time model change and weak wedding calendar.

segments.name: Adjacencies (footwear, innerwear and others)
segments.commentary: Adjacent categories grew 25% and now make up about 24% of business. Stride has 19 stores.

segments.name: Wholesale and department stores
segments.commentary: Delivered strong double-digit secondary sales growth in Q4.

guidance_outlook: FY27: sustain mid-double-digit revenue growth, with management citing about 15% and about 7-8% like-for-like growth split roughly equally between price and volume.
FY27: 30-40 bps EBITDA margin expansion, guided despite a more uncertain macro.
Net-debt-zero target now in about 9-12 months; apart from the Flipkart-related borrowing, debt is expected to fall year-on-year.
Store additions: about 1.5 lakh net sq ft of space expected in FY27; around 5% of stores expected to close going forward.
Longer term: take gross margin toward the high 50s over 2-3 years; take D2C share of sales to 65%.
Each brand expected to have its own dotcom and app live in FY27; flyingmachine.com to launch in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR110 crore, covering store investments including deposits for about 50 COCO stores opened in the year, MBO and department store investment, and IT and admin spend.
FY26 added more than 1.4 lakh net sq ft of retail space; FY27 plans about 1.5 lakh net sq ft addition across the portfolio.
Company reorganised into a business unit structure and set up a dedicated tech and AI team over the last two quarters.
Inventory turns expected to move to 3.7-3.8x from 4.0x as channel mix shifts toward D2C.
demand_pricing: Demand environment described as stable; government measures on GST, interest rates and income tax supported demand; West Asia situation flagged as a watch item.
Management expects mild pressure on raw materials, forex and capex, and a possible consumption slowdown from supply-led inflation; SS26 inventory bought early to lock costs, AW26 being hedged.
Management says sourcing remains predominantly India-based and will be deepened; selective price increases planned while protecting growth.
Premiumisation trend seen across all brands quarter on quarter; online competition described as stabilising.
Store closures expected at about 5% going forward, not concentrated in one brand.

qa_highlights.question: Will U.S. Polo keep growing at its recent pace, and how will brand-wise growth look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said U.S. Polo has reached its potential, PVH brands will keep growing, and Flying Machine should sustain solid double-digit growth. It guided to mid-double-digit growth across brands rather than a brand-specific CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: Can 30-40 bps margin expansion hold with cotton prices rising and A&P spend increasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India-based sourcing, cost-control measures, selective price increases and mitigation already in motion. It said it is cautious but optimistic on the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are inventory days up about 20 days over two years, and how many COCO stores were closed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed inventory days mainly to channel mix shift toward D2C, which holds inventory on books. Early SS26 inwards were made ahead of geopolitical delays, and creditors offset part of the build. The CFO did not have the COCO closure count and offered to follow up offline.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to fund debt reduction and what is the acceptances position?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt rose in the quarter due to borrowing for the Flipkart transaction. Cash generation will go first to term loan repayment, then to working capital financing; acceptances are used to manage MSME payables and are reported in the annual report.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8% retail LTL for the full network or COCO only, and how is it measured?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said LTL is based on consumer data across the full network. The company operates on a consignment basis for its stores, and sales are recorded when the final consumer buys.

risks_watch: Inventory rose more than 30% YoY in FY26 against 15% revenue growth; inventory days are up about 20 days over two years, and management attributes this to channel mix and early inwards.
Raw material, forex and capex pressure from the West Asia situation and cotton price uptrend could hit the 30-40 bps margin guidance.
Possible consumption slowdown from inflation; management has not quantified price increase elasticity.
Arrow subdued in Q4 (one-time model change, weak wedding calendar); the brand's recovery is still to be proven.
Flipkart transaction borrowing lifted debt in Q4; net-debt-zero target in 9-12 months depends on cash generation.
Reserves fell about INR13 crore YoY due to an equity adjustment linked to the Flipkart transaction.
Disclosure gaps: no brand-wise numbers, no full-price sales mix, and no COCO closure count given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance, though cautious on macro, raw material and forex risk. Management was less precise on inventory build, store closure counts and brand-level numbers, deferring some answers offline.
key_quotes: We expect to sustain mid -double-digit growth with another 30 -40 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion, despite a more uncertain macro.
Our D2C engine is compounding. Direct channels now account for 56% of sales, up 300 basis points year-on-year.
Our brands have actually premiumized while at the same time ensuring great value at fabulous prices.
